metadata.case_name: LEE PO FOON v. AU CHI KIN

plaintiff.occupation_before: clerk at the dental clinic of North District Hospital (civil servant)

source: The record of finding on admission revealed she suffered from right forehead haematoma.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of other or unspecified sites of head

source: The doctor recorded a diagnosis of minor head injury, she was given symptomatic treatment and the prognosis was ‘good with minimal permanent disability’.

In Dr. Chung’s opinion, Madam Lee is prone to developing depression whenever she is under stress due to her pre-existing dysthymic disorder. After the accident, she suffered from (1) post concussional disorder with impairment in cognitive functioning accompanied by specific neuro behavioural symptoms that occurred as a consequence of closed head injury concussion.

injuries.description: minor neck sprain with soft tissue injury
source: Madam Lee (a) had a neck injury at the accident which should be a minor neck sprain with soft tissue injury which had recovered at the time of examination;
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

source: (b) scapular pain due to a sprain or contusion of the region during the accident. No sign of shoulder joint involvement found.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of other or unspecified parts of shoulder girdle

source: Madam Lee complained that she had suffered contusion in the right shoulder and thigh and whiplash in the cervical spine at the accident.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of shoulder or upper arm

source: Madam Lee complained that she had suffered contusion in the right shoulder and thigh and whiplash in the cervical spine at the accident.

injuries.description: TMJ derangement with anterior disc displacement on the right side
source: Dr. K.F. Chow reported after a MRI scan of Madam Lee’s TMJ on 20 March 2007 the following: “TMJ derangement with anterior disc displacement on the right side. Diagnostic arthroscopy was suggested ….… preferred to continue with the conservative treatment.”
injuries.icd_description: Dislocation or sprain of other specified joints or ligaments of head

injuries.description: recurrent depressive disorder / relapse of dysthymic disorder
source: On 2 February 2007, Dr. H.B. Lam of Shatin Hospital reported that Madam Lee’s mood and sleep had improved but had difficulty with her memory. His diagnosis of Madam Lee was “recurrent depressive disorder” and the differential diagnosis was “post-concussional syndrome”.

injuries.description: major depressive disorder (diagnosis by Dr. Leo Chiu)
source: Madam Lee consulted a private psychiatrist Dr. Leo Chiu for her depressed mood and insomnia on 25 April 2007, his diagnosis was “major depressive disorder”.

manifestations.description: TMJ clicking and recurrent facial pain
anxiety when traveling in motor vehicles

treatments_received.treatment: admitted to the Prince of Wales Hospital neurological ward for observation
source: After the accident, Madam Lee was admitted to the Prince of Wales Hospital neurological ward (“PWH”) for 2 days after the initial examination at the Accident and Emergency Department at 22:02 hours on the night of the accident.

treatments_received.treatment: symptomatic treatment for minor head injury
source: The doctor recorded a diagnosis of minor head injury, she was given symptomatic treatment and the prognosis was ‘good with minimal permanent disability’.
Madam Lee was treated orthopaedically for her right shoulder and neck injuries on 29 occasions and received 29 sessions of physiotherapy.
she consulted orthopaedic surgeon Dr. Baldwin Chan at the Union Hospital and received physiotherapy treatments at the Union Hospital.
She further received 20 sessions of acupuncture
and 15 bonesetter’s treatments.

treatments_received.treatment: botox injection to right and left masseter muscles
source: Dr. Chow treated her with botox injection to relieve the pain at the right and left masseter muscles.
Dr. K.F. Chow reported after a MRI scan of Madam Lee’s TMJ on 20 March 2007 the following: “TMJ derangement with anterior disc displacement on the right side."
She received physiotherapy at the Union Hospital and hydrotherapy at the PWH.
She attended Dr. H.B. Lam’s psychiatric clinic on 22 September 2006 complaining of depressed mood, poor memory and fragmented sleep.
Madam Lee consulted a private psychiatrist Dr. Leo Chiu for her depressed mood and insomnia on 25 April 2007...

treatments_future.treatment: 12 months of psychological treatment (monthly psychological treatment for 1 year)
source: Dr. Chung recommended Madam Lee to receive 12 months of treatments for her mental condition which he assessed will cost $25,000.

losses.description: developed poor marital relationship with her husband.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: had to hire a helper on Sundays, the day her domestic helper was on leave.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: anxiety when traveling in motor vehicles.
difficulty in concentration and poor memory.

comparable_cases.case_name: Yau Kwok Yue v. Dong Shu Kei Beau
comparable_cases.injury_description: 35 year old plaintiff sustained injuries to his head and back; 19 months after the attack still suffering from depressed mood, poor sleep, lacking in concentration and interests; diagnosed with post-traumatic disorder, post concussional syndrome and depressive disorder.
